references.text: The glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud, a parallel to the promise that the glory of the Lord would appear for the people
The glory of the Lord rested on Mount Sinai and appeared to the children of Israel, the same theme of God's glorious revelation
The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle, fulfilling the promise that God's glory would be revealed
Fulfillment of the promise in verse 6, where the glory of the Lord actually appeared for all the people
The glory of the Lord appeared in the tent of meeting to all the children of Israel
The cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord was revealed
The glory of the Lord appeared to Moses and Aaron at the tent of meeting
The glory of the Lord fills the temple, an eschatological fulfillment of God's glorious revelation
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory – the ultimate revelation of God's glory
Jesus revealed his glory through signs, a New Testament parallel to God's glorious revelation
